item.title: BACK IN HISTORY | Weavers learn skills

item.content:encoded:
Two Fijian weavers returned from New Zealand with new techniques after attending the first international symposium for indigenous weavers.

The Fiji Times reported on Thursday, April 29, 1993, that the two — Adi Silika Marama, a master weaver from Wailevu Village in Cakaudrove, and Seniloli Sovea, a contemporary weaver of Suva — attended the symposium in Papakura, Auckland. The New Zealand High Commission funded their trip.

The symposium was the first of its kind and brought together experts in indigenous weaving from North America, the Pacific Rim, and the South Pacific region. The event was arranged to mark the International Year of Indigenous Peoples, which the United Nations had declared for 1993.

During the 12-day program, participants exchanged ideas and experiences through seminars and practical workshops. Craftspeople shared their techniques, designs, styles, and demonstrated how traditional knowledge was passed down through generations.

For Adi Silika, who was recognised in her village as a keeper of traditional weaving methods, the symposium provided an opportunity to observe how different cultures prepared and preserved fibres.

For Mrs Sovea, whose work reflected a more contemporary style based in an urban setting, it was an opportunity to see how ancient designs had been adapted for modern use.

Both women said they had learned new weaving styles and would be able to teach those techniques to other weavers in Fiji. They demonstrated the fine mats and baskets distinctive to Cakaudrove and explained the significance of patterns representing family and vanua ties.

They also learned about the methods Māori weavers used to treat raw fibres and prepare them for weaving. This included preparing New Zealand flax, known as harakeke, which was stripped, softened, and coloured with natural dyes.

Officials of the Fiji Arts Council said the exchange was valuable for cultural preservation. At the time, concerns had been raised that younger generations were losing interest in weaving because of the availability of goods. Programs such as the symposium helped renew pride in handmade crafts.

item.title: Trio front court on illicit drug charge
item.description: THREE people appeared in court last week on separate cases of alleged unlawful possession of illicit drugs, namely methamphetamine and cocaine. According to a police statement, the three, Sanjesh Chand, Roneel Kumar and Praneeta Kumar, were arrested as part of joint taskforce efforts in partnership with the Republic of Fiji Military Forces.
item.content:encoded:
THREE people appeared in court last week on separate cases of alleged unlawful possession of illicit drugs, namely methamphetamine and cocaine.

According to a police statement, the three, Sanjesh Chand, Roneel Kumar and Praneeta Kumar, were arrested as part of joint taskforce efforts in partnership with the Republic of Fiji Military Forces.

“In the first raid conducted on the July 23, 2026, at Naikabula, Lautoka, the suspect was arrested following the discovery of two plastics containing crystals confirmed to be cocaine weighing 45.2 grams and $3155 in cash,” police said.

“The accused (Chand) was charged and produced at the Lautoka Magistrate’s Court and remanded at the Natabua Corrections Centre.”

The police statement said the second raid conducted on July 28 at Sabeto, Nadi, plastic bags of white crystals confirmed to be methamphetamine weighing 21.3 grams, dried leaves tested positive for marijuana and $4850 cash were seized.

“A couple (Roneel Kumar and Praneeta Kumar) was arrested at the residence. They were charged and produced at the Nadi Magistrate’s Court on Friday, July 31, 2026, and remanded at the Natabua Corrections Centre.

“The case will be recalled on August 5, 2026.”

According to police, the estimated street value of both seizures was more than $23,000.

item.title: Man acquitted of attempted murder charge
item.description: A MAN accused of attempting to murder his 70-year-old father with a cane knife has been acquitted of the charge but convicted of the lesser offence of unlawfully and maliciously causing grievous harm. item.content:encoded:
A MAN accused of attempting to murder his 70-year-old father with a cane knife has been acquitted of the charge but convicted of the lesser offence of unlawfully and maliciously causing grievous harm.

Arone Vonosewa was found not guilty of the charge of murder after Justice Siainiu Fa’alogo-Bull ruled that the prosecution had failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that he intended to kill his father, Mario Nasoro, during an incident at Masi Village on August 23, 2024.

The court heard that the incident arose from a domestic dispute involving Vonosewa, his younger brother and their father. After a physical altercation inside the family home, Vonosewa struck his father with a knife, causing a 12-centimetre laceration to the back of his head, damage to a tendon in his middle finger and bruising to his back.

The State argued that Vonosewa intended to kill his father, relying on the nature of the weapon, the injuries sustained and evidence that threats had been made during the confrontation.

However, Justice Bull found the evidence did not establish an intention to cause death.

Evidence also showed that blows to the victim’s back were delivered with the blunt side of the blade and that Vonosewa stopped the attack when instructed to do so.

While acquitting Vonosewa of attempted murder, the court found he had deliberately and unlawfully caused serious injuries to his father.

item.title: Magistrate vacates trial date
item.description: THE November trial of Carpenters Fiji Ltd’s managing director Daniel Whippy and former National Fire Authority’s board chairman John O’Connor has been vacated and will be rescheduled for 2027. Magistrate Sufia Hamza informed the parties yesterday the three-week trial could not be accommodated within the available timeframe because of an upcoming judicial workshop and the large number of witnesses
item.content:encoded:
THE November trial of Carpenters Fiji Ltd’s managing director Daniel Whippy and former National Fire Authority’s board chairman John O’Connor has been vacated and will be rescheduled for 2027.

Magistrate Sufia Hamza informed the parties yesterday the three-week trial could not be accommodated within the available timeframe because of an upcoming judicial workshop and the large number of witnesses expected to be called.

A new trial date will be fixed on September 3 when the matter is next called.

Mr O’Connor is charged with one count of abuse of office for gain, while Mr Whippy faces one count of counselling the commission of an offence.

The duo are alleged to have amended the findings of the investigations into the MH Warehouse fire at Walu Bay in Suva in April of 2018.

In an earlier court appearance, FICAC indicated it intended to call 38 witnesses, while the defence is expected to call six witnesses, including the two accused.

item.content:encoded:
A MAGISTRATE has directed parties in the four-day trial of former finance minister Professor Biman Prasad to ensure the proceedings begin and conclude “smoothly”, with all outstanding disclosure issues resolved before the hearing starts next week.

During a pretrial conference yesterday, Magistrate Yogesh Prasad instructed senior FICAC prosecutor Joseph Work to provide the defence with the prosecution’s witness list by tomorrow.

Prof Prasad faces one count of failure to comply with statutory disclosure requirements and one count of providing false information in a statutory declaration in 2015.

The prosecution intends to call four witnesses during the trial, which is scheduled to commence on Monday next week.

The matter has been adjourned to August 7.

item.title: Court jails rapist dad
item.description: A 56-YEAR-OLD married man was sentenced to 11 years and nine months in prison for raping his 11-year-old daughter. Justice Siainiu Fa’alogo-Bull sentenced the father-of-two on July 17 after he pleaded guilty to a count of rape committed on April 7 this year.
item.content:encoded:
A 56-YEAR-OLD married man was sentenced to 11 years and nine months in prison for raping his 11-year-old daughter.

Justice Siainiu Fa’alogo-Bull sentenced the father-of-two on July 17 after he pleaded guilty to a count of rape committed on April 7 this year.

The court heard that on the day in question, the victim had returned from a shower and was getting dressed when her father approached her, grabbed her hand, and forced her onto the mattress, where he sexually violated her.

He was caught in the act by his wife, who returned home unexpectedly and immediately reported the matter to the police.

Justice Bull condemned the man’s actions, stating that he robbed her of her innocence by exposing her to sexual acts at such a young age.

“By sexually violating her, you abused your authority as a father and breached the sacred trust reposed in you,” the judge ruled.

The man will be eligible for parole after serving 10 years of his head sentence.

In a separate case, a 63-year-old man has been sentenced to five years, five months, and 20 days’ in jail for sexually assaulting his 13-year-old granddaughter in 2019.

Magistrate Timoci Qalinauci imposed a non-parole period of four years when sentencing the man at the Rakiraki Magistrate’s on Friday last week.

During trial, the court was told the victim went to her grandfather’s home to ask for broomsticks, where the man committed the act despite her repeated requests for him to stop.

The victim escaped and reported the incident to a relative. Her mother confronted the accused the following day and lodged a report with the police.

Magistrate Qalinauci said the man’s action would traumatise the victim for the rest of her life.

“Children need to feel safe when they are at home with family members or relatives, and they should know that a home is their sanctuary and it is a space that they must feel safe and protected from any form of harm,” he said.

item.title: Kamikamica sworn back in as Deputy Prime Minister
item.description: Manoa Kamikamica has officially returned to Government, taking the oath of office as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises at State House today. President Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu presided over the swearing-in ceremony, which was attended by Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka and members of Mr Kamikamica’s family.
item.content:encoded:
Manoa Kamikamica has officially returned to Government, taking the oath of office as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises at State House today.

President Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu presided over the swearing-in ceremony, which was attended by Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka and members of Mr Kamikamica’s family.

During the ceremony, Mr Kamikamica took the Oath of Allegiance and the Oath of Due Execution of Office, formally resuming his ministerial responsibilities.

His return comes after the Suva Magistrates Court dismissed the criminal case against him, acquitting him on charges of perjury and providing false information to a public servant after ruling there was no case to answer.

As Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises, he is expected to resume oversight of key sectors aimed at promoting investment, supporting business growth and advancing Government’s economic development agenda.

Public enterprises was under Minister Charan Jeath Singh until now.

His reinstatement restores him to the position of Deputy Prime Minister alongside his ministerial portfolio.

item.title: Bench warrant issued for former teacher over alleged abusive video
item.description: A Bench warrant has been issued against former schoolteacher, who is accused of posting a video in which he uttered abusive words towards the Minister for Employment, Productivity and Industrial Relations, Agni Deo Singh, in 2022. Mr Kumar failed to appear before Magistrate Sufia Hamza, who subsequently issued the warrant.
item.content:encoded:
A Bench warrant has been issued against former schoolteacher, who is accused of posting a video in which he uttered abusive words towards the Minister for Employment, Productivity and Industrial Relations, Agni Deo Singh, in 2022.

Mr Kumar failed to appear before Magistrate Sufia Hamza, who subsequently issued the warrant.

It is alleged that on December 14, two years ago, Mr Kumar, while in the Suva Magistrate’s Court, secured access to a Facebook account which did not belong to him and used it to post a video on a social media platform titled ‘Power In His Voice’.

He is accused of uttering vulgarities against Mr Singh, who was the Fiji Teachers Union general secretary at the time.

The case has been adjourned to November 13.
